scenes.tts: If the brain keeps its gene, can changing the first touch neuron still change a mouse's response? A gentle air puff bends hairs on the back. A gold sensory neuron carries the signal through a teal spinal cord toward a blue brain. The mouse's movement becomes our readout.
scenes.visual: Hook first. Fill the frame with a side-on mouse skin cross-section, a gold sensory neuron, a teal spinal-cord block and a blue brain block. A white puff bends three hairs, then a pulse travels along the neuron. A large red movement gauge rises beside a mouse silhouette. Keep every block moving subtly. Label the gauge 'movement, schematic'.
scenes.narration: If the brain keeps its gene, can changing the first touch neuron still change a mouse's response? A gentle air puff bends hairs on the back. A gold sensory neuron carries the signal through a teal spinal cord toward a blue brain. The mouse's movement becomes our readout.

scenes.tts: In these mouse experiments, a fixed air puff measured movement, not perception. The puff stays constant while the movement gauge changes. That differs from a detection threshold. It also cannot tell us how the animal experiences touch.
scenes.visual: Keep the same pathway. Lock the puff control with a visible padlock. Repeat two identical puffs while the red movement gauge reaches different heights. Transform the gauge into two labels: 'fixed stimulus' and 'movement'. Briefly show a crossed-out speech bubble beside the mouse to mark that experience was not measured.
scenes.narration: In these mouse experiments, a fixed air puff measured movement, not perception. The puff stays constant while the movement gauge changes. That differs from a detection threshold. It also cannot tell us how the animal experiences touch.

scenes.tts: Now place a gene badge in every cell. Advillin Cree removes a floxed gene from dorsal-root and trigeminal sensory neurons. The driver also reaches sympathetic ganglion neurons. Resident spinal and brain cells keep their badges. The sensory neuron's central terminal does not.
scenes.caption: Now place a gene badge in every cell. Advillin-Cre removes a floxed gene from dorsal-root and trigeminal sensory neurons. The driver also reaches sympathetic ganglion neurons. Resident spinal and brain cells keep their badges. The sensory neuron's central terminal does not.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the carried pathway at the same positions. Gold gene badges appear in the sensory neuron, teal resident spinal cells and blue brain cells. A labelled 'Advillin-Cre' selector sweeps along the entire gold neuron and removes only its badge, including at the terminal inside the cord. The teal and blue badges remain bright.
scenes.narration: Now place a gene badge in every cell. Advillin-Cre removes a floxed gene from dorsal-root and trigeminal sensory neurons. The driver also reaches sympathetic ganglion neurons. Resident spinal and brain cells keep their badges. The sensory neuron's central terminal does not.

scenes.tts: Deleting M E C P two or G A B R B three occurs only in that targeted population. The resident central nervous system copies remain intact. If the first neuron contributes to the measured outcome, what should happen after the restricted deletion?
scenes.caption: Deleting Mecp2 or Gabrb3 occurs only in that targeted population. The resident central nervous system copies remain intact. If the first neuron contributes to the measured outcome, what should happen after the restricted deletion?
scenes.visual: Show two large gene chips, 'Mecp2' and 'Gabrb3', entering the Advillin-Cre selector one at a time. The gold neuron's badge disappears each time. Keep the fixed puff control ready, but leave the red movement gauge empty with a question mark. Hold the question large and central at the end.
scenes.narration: Deleting Mecp2 or Gabrb3 occurs only in that targeted population. The resident central nervous system copies remain intact. If the first neuron contributes to the measured outcome, what should happen after the restricted deletion?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Keep the pathway, fixed-puff icon and empty movement gauge visible. A slow pulse travels from skin to cord every two seconds. Keep the question on screen without revealing the result.

scenes.tts: The response became stronger. Texture discrimination and tactile prepulse inhibition also changed. Developmental deletion shifted selected anxiety-like and social-interaction assays. Gene loss in the Advillin-targeted population was sufficient for selected mouse outcomes. Sufficient does not mean exclusive.
scenes.visual: Repeat the identical puff. Animate the red movement gauge higher than its control outline. Three outcome tiles grow from that gauge: 'air-puff response', 'texture task' and 'selected assays'. Stamp 'sufficient for these outcomes' across the gold neuron, then split the stamp so 'not exclusive' remains visible beneath it. All gauges are labelled 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The response became stronger. Texture discrimination and tactile prepulse inhibition also changed. Developmental deletion shifted selected anxiety-like and social-interaction assays. Gene loss in the Advillin-targeted population was sufficient for selected mouse outcomes. Sufficient does not mean exclusive.

scenes.tts: The reverse test started with an otherwise null mouse. Researchers restored M E C P two mainly in the Advillin-targeted population. Tactile sensitivity and selected anxiety-like and social measures shifted toward control. Lethality, memory deficits and motor deficits did not.
scenes.caption: The reverse test started with an otherwise null mouse. Researchers restored Mecp2 mainly in the Advillin-targeted population. Tactile sensitivity and selected anxiety-like and social measures shifted toward control. Lethality, memory deficits and motor deficits did not.
scenes.visual: Dim every gene badge to show the otherwise-null background, then restore one bright badge along the gold Advillin-targeted neuron. Outcome tiles physically sort into two columns. Green-outlined tiles for tactile and selected behavioural measures slide toward a control marker. Red-outlined lethality, memory and motor tiles remain in place. Label all motion 'assay outcomes'.
scenes.narration: The reverse test started with an otherwise null mouse. Researchers restored Mecp2 mainly in the Advillin-targeted population. Tactile sensitivity and selected anxiety-like and social measures shifted toward control. Lethality, memory deficits and motor deficits did not.

scenes.tts: Restoring Mecp2 mainly in that population rescued selected outcomes but left others unchanged. The rescue therefore draws a boundary around the claim. A peripheral sensory neuron can contribute to part of this mouse phenotype. It does not explain every feature, or establish the same mechanism in people.
scenes.visual: Draw a gold boundary around the rescued tiles and sensory neuron, leaving the unchanged tiles and blue brain outside. The boundary becomes a bracket labelled 'one contribution'. Fade in a human outline beyond a dashed gap labelled 'not tested here'. Finish by returning to the whole skin-to-brain pathway.
scenes.narration: Restoring Mecp2 mainly in that population rescued selected outcomes but left others unchanged. The rescue therefore draws a boundary around the claim. A peripheral sensory neuron can contribute to part of this mouse phenotype. It does not explain every feature, or establish the same mechanism in people.

scenes.tts: Now gather what those restricted tests earned. A restricted manipulation can locate one contribution without explaining the whole phenotype. Keep the full pathway in view, and ask exactly which cells each experiment changed.
scenes.visual: Keep the complete pathway large. Three concise take-home labels transform in sequence from the existing objects: 'restricted cells', 'selected outcomes', 'bounded inference'. The gold neuron glows, while teal spinal and blue brain blocks remain visible. End with the whole pathway, not a list.
scenes.narration: Now gather what those restricted tests earned. A restricted manipulation can locate one contribution without explaining the whole phenotype. Keep the full pathway in view, and ask exactly which cells each experiment changed.

scenes.tts: This logic does not ask whether the brain matters. It asks whether one targeted population can move one measured outcome while other cells remain unchanged. The answer is bounded by the cells, assay, species and developmental schedule.
scenes.visual: Hold the complete pathway. A spotlight circles the gold targeted population, then a second outline encloses the movement gauge. Four boundary labels orbit slowly without becoming a list: 'cells', 'assay', 'species', 'time'. The teal spinal and blue brain regions remain active in the background.
scenes.narration: This logic does not ask whether the brain matters. It asks whether one targeted population can move one measured outcome while other cells remain unchanged. The answer is bounded by the cells, assay, species and developmental schedule.

scenes.visual: End card over the carried pathway. Large line, no more than twelve words: 'A restricted test locates one contribution, not the whole phenotype.' Let a slow pulse continue along the gold neuron.
